objectives.statement: Describe the formal structure of the Spanish Constitution of 1978 and distinguish its main normative divisions.
objectives.citation: Constitution structure: Preamble, Preliminary Title, Titles I-X and additional, transitional, repealing and final provisions

objectives.statement: Explain the constitutional definition of Spain as a social and democratic State under the rule of law and identify the constitutional form of government.
Relate the constitutional principles of national unity, autonomy of nationalities and regions, and solidarity.
Identify the constitutional language rules concerning Spanish, the other official languages and linguistic heritage.
Compare the binding principles imposed on public authorities by legality, legal certainty, responsibility and the prohibition of arbitrariness.
Explain human dignity, inviolable rights and free development of personality as the foundation of political order and social peace.
Apply the constitutional equality and non-discrimination rule to the grounds expressly listed in the Constitution.
Distinguish the constitutional protection of the right to life and physical and moral integrity from prohibited torture and inhuman or degrading treatment.
Explain the scope and limits of ideological, religious and worship freedom under the Constitution.
Apply the constitutional safeguards for personal liberty, including the maximum ordinary period of detention before release or judicial appearance.
Relate privacy, honour, personal and family intimacy, home inviolability and secrecy of communications as distinct constitutional guarantees.
Compare the freedoms protected by the constitutional communication and expression guarantee, including the prohibition of prior censorship.
Identify the constitutional requirements for exercising the right of peaceful and unarmed assembly.
Apply the right to participate in public affairs directly or through freely elected representatives and to access public functions on equal terms.
Analyze the constitutional elements of effective judicial protection and the prohibition of indefensión.
Explain the constitutional right to education and distinguish its purposes from the freedom to teach.
Analyze the constitutional recognition of trade-union freedom and the right to strike, including legally established limits.
Apply the principles of generality, equality, ability to pay and progressivity to the constitutional tax system.
Explain the representative role of the Cortes Generales and distinguish Congress and Senate as the two constitutional chambers.
Distinguish organic laws from ordinary laws by their reserved subject matter and approval requirement.
